analysis.investment_thesis: KSB is a genuinely good business with ~24.5% ROIC and zero debt, but at an earnings yield of only ~2.2% (EBIT ₹374 Cr / EV ~₹16,688 Cr), the Magic Formula ranks it near the bottom on cheapness. Quality at this price is not a bargain — it's a speculation on multiple expansion.
key_strengths: ROIC ~24.5% (ROCE given) sustained over multiple years — passes the Magic Formula quality threshold comfortably
Virtually debt-free balance sheet (D/E = 0.00, borrowings ₹5 Cr) with cash of ₹167 Cr — fortress-like
Consistent revenue CAGR of 14% and net profit CAGR of 16.4% over 9 years — durable compounder
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2.2% (EBIT/EV) is catastrophically low vs my 12%+ threshold — paying 58x P/E for ~14% growth implies PEG >4x
FCF is erratic: ₹0 in 2025 and negative in 2022 despite strong reported profits — capex (~₹94-107 Cr/yr) and working capital absorb nearly all earnings
Other income (₹48 Cr, ~18% of operating profit) inflates headline PAT — strip it out and quality of earnings is lower than it appears
red_flags: Earnings yield ~2.2% — far below my 6% minimum floor; Magic Formula rejects this outright on cheapness
Free cash flow was ₹0 in FY2025 and negative in FY2022 despite ₹270 Cr net profit — FCF conversion is poor
EV/EBITDA of 44.4x for a mid-teens growth industrial company prices in perfection for a decade
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on KSB: EBIT = ₹374 Cr (FY2025 operating income), EV = Market Cap ₹16,850 + Debt ₹5 − Cash ₹167 = ~₹16,688 Cr. Earnings Yield = 374/16,688 = **2.2%** — an automatic disqualifier. ROIC using EBIT / (NWC + Net Fixed Assets) proxied by ROCE comes in at ~24.5%, which is genuinely good and clears my 20% hurdle. But the Magic Formula requires BOTH metrics to rank well. With earnings yield in the bottom decile of any universe, this stock fails the formula decisively regardless of quality.

The business itself is admirable — a German-pedigreed industrial compounder with zero debt, 69.8% promoter commitment, and secular exposure to water/wastewater capex in India. But the market knows all of this and has priced it at 58x trailing earnings and 44x EBITDA. FCF generation is the hidden concern: despite ₹270 Cr net profit in FY2025, free cash flow was ₹0 — capex of ₹94 Cr plus working capital build consumed every rupee. Until the stock trades at an earnings yield of at least 8-10% (implying a price closer to ₹350-450), the Magic Formula says wait.
